questions.stem: A state in India (i) shares international borders with 3 countries, (ii) contains the confluence of the Teesta with the Brahmaputra system's tributaries, and (iii) hosts the Kanchenjunga National Park — a UNESCO mixed (natural + cultural) World Heritage Site. Identify the state.
questions.explanation: Sikkim borders Nepal, Bhutan and China (3 countries). Teesta (with Rangit tributary) runs through it. Khangchendzonga National Park is UNESCO Mixed-Heritage (2016). Arunachal borders 3 countries too (China, Bhutan, Myanmar) but does not host Kanchenjunga. Three-clue identification.

questions.stem: Consider the following statements about Indian RIVERS. 1. The Godavari rises in the Western Ghats near Trimbak and drains into the Bay of Bengal. 2. The Narmada flows eastward into the Bay of Bengal. 3. The Kaveri enters the Bay of Bengal at Poompuhar in Tamil Nadu. 4. Among peninsular rivers, the Krishna has the longest course inside Indian territory. Which statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement 2 is WRONG — Narmada flows WEST into the Arabian Sea via the Gulf of Khambhat (via a rift valley between Vindhya and Satpura). Statement 4 is WRONG — the longest peninsular river IN India is the Godavari (~1,465 km), not Krishna (~1,400 km). Statements 1 and 3 are correct.

questions.stem: Match List-I (Himalayan peak) with List-II (state / location in India). A. Kanchenjunga. B. Nanda Devi. C. Nun Kun. D. Saramati. List-II: 1. Nagaland. 2. Uttarakhand. 3. Sikkim. 4. Jammu & Kashmir / Ladakh.
questions.explanation: Kanchenjunga (8,586 m) — Sikkim-Nepal border, India's highest peak entirely on Indian soil is Nanda Devi in Uttarakhand (7,816 m). Nun Kun massif in Ladakh region. Saramati (3,826 m) — highest peak of Nagaland and of the Naga Hills. Pan-India peak tour: must-know matching for UPSC/SSC.

questions.stem: Arrange the following tributaries of the GANGA in the order in which they JOIN the Ganga, moving from upstream to downstream (west to east). 1. Gomti. 2. Yamuna. 3. Kosi. 4. Son.
questions.explanation: Yamuna joins Ganga at Prayagraj (Sangam, UP). Gomti joins at Saidpur in Ghazipur (UP, downstream of Prayagraj). Son joins at Patna (Bihar). Kosi joins near Kursela (Katihar, Bihar) — further east. Order: Yamuna → Gomti → Son → Kosi.

questions.stem: Which of the following pairs of a PASS and its HIMALAYAN STATE is INCORRECT?
questions.explanation: Bum La lies in ARUNACHAL PRADESH (on the India-China / Tibet border, north of Tawang), NOT Uttarakhand. Zoji La connects Srinagar to Leh; Nathu La links Sikkim to Tibet (trade route); Shipki La in Kinnaur district of HP. Negative-stem pair-check.

questions.stem: A tropical cyclone forms over the Bay of Bengal and moves toward the Odisha coast. Which of the following factors does NOT contribute to its intensification?

options.option_text: Presence of the Coriolis force at sufficient latitude (> ~5° N)
High vertical wind shear in the troposphere

questions.explanation: HIGH vertical wind shear DISRUPTS cyclone structure and INHIBITS intensification. Low shear is what a cyclone needs. The other three (warm SST >26.5°C, adequate Coriolis, pre-existing disturbance) are textbook necessary conditions. 'Which does NOT contribute' — negative-stem test of mechanism.

questions.stem: ASSERTION (A): The Western Ghats receive orographic rainfall from the South-West Monsoon on their western (windward) slopes, but the Deccan interior lies in a rain shadow. REASON (R): Moisture-laden winds rising over the Ghats cool and condense; by the time air descends on the leeward side it has lost most of its moisture and warms adiabatically.

options.option_text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

questions.explanation: Classic orographic + rain-shadow mechanism. Mahabaleshwar, Agumbe (west of Ghats) > 500 cm annual rainfall; Solapur, Pune-east in the rain shadow < 70 cm. The adiabatic mechanism in R is the exact physical explanation of A.

questions.stem: Consider the following about the SUNDARBANS. 1. It is the world's largest tidal halophytic (mangrove) forest. 2. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site (1987) AND a Ramsar Site (2019). 3. The Indian Sundarbans lies entirely in West Bengal. 4. The Royal Bengal Tiger here is the only tiger population adapted to swim and hunt in saline tidal water. Which are correct?
questions.explanation: All four statements are correct. Sundarbans Delta spans India (West Bengal) and Bangladesh; the Indian portion is entirely in West Bengal's South 24 Parganas (and part of North 24 Parganas). Sundarbans National Park: UNESCO 1987. Sundarbans Wetland: Ramsar 2019 (India's largest Ramsar site). Sundarbans tigers are famed swimmers and regularly hunt in the saline creeks.

questions.stem: Regarding the BHABAR zone found in the Himalayan foothills, which of the following statements is CORRECT?

options.option_text: It lies south of Terai and is permanently waterlogged and marshy
It is a narrow belt of porous gravel where stream water seeps underground
It extends into the Indo-Gangetic Plain and is the most fertile zone
It receives the highest rainfall among all Himalayan foot-hill zones

questions.explanation: Bhabar is a narrow, porous gravel-and-boulder zone at the base of the Siwaliks where streams descend and lose their water by percolating through the coarse bed. They re-emerge as springs and swamps in the Terai, which lies south of Bhabar — not the reverse as stated in Option A, which is the most common confusion candidates make.

questions.stem: Which of the following is India's ONLY ACTIVE VOLCANO?

options.option_text: Barren Island, located in the Andaman & Nicobar group
Narcondam Island, located in the Andaman & Nicobar group
Minicoy Island, located in the southern Lakshadweep group
Pamban Island, located in the Gulf of Mannar off Tamil Nadu

questions.explanation: Barren Island in the Andaman & Nicobar group is India's only active volcano, with eruptions recorded as recently as 2017. Narcondam, the classic distractor, is in the same island group but is classified as dormant/extinct, not active. Minicoy (Lakshadweep) and Pamban are coral and sedimentary islands, respectively, with no volcanic activity.

questions.stem:
Consider the following statements about LATERITE SOIL in India:
1. It is formed by intense leaching under heavy rainfall and high temperatures.
2. It is rich in iron and aluminium but deficient in nitrogen, phosphorus, and potash.
3. It is the dominant soil type in the Indo-Gangetic Plains.
Which of the above statements is/are CORRECT?
questions.explanation: Laterite soil forms through intense leaching — heavy tropical rain dissolves silica and flushes it away, leaving an iron- and aluminium-oxide-rich residue (Statements 1 and 2 are correct). Statement 3 is false: the Indo-Gangetic Plains are dominated by deep alluvial soils, not laterite. Laterite is found mainly in Karnataka, Kerala, parts of Tamil Nadu, Odisha, and the Northeast hill regions.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the PRINCIPAL REASON why the Western Coastal Plains of India are much narrower than the Eastern Coastal Plains?

options.option_text: The Western Ghats run close and parallel to the coast, restricting the plain's width
The Arabian Sea is deeper than the Bay of Bengal, limiting sediment accumulation
Fewer rivers drain westward, resulting in lesser alluvial deposition along the coast
Tectonic uplift along the western margin has raised the coastal terrain significantly

questions.explanation: The Western Ghats run almost parallel to the west coast at distances of only 30–50 km, leaving a narrow strip averaging 10–25 km for the Konkan and Malabar plains. The Eastern Coastal Plains (Coromandel and Northern Circars) are 80–100 km wide because the Eastern Ghats are discontinuous and set far from the coast. Option B is factually wrong — the Arabian Sea continental shelf is actually shallower than that of the Bay of Bengal.

questions.stem: Which region lies in the RAIN SHADOW of the Western Ghats and therefore receives less than 700 mm of annual rainfall despite being geographically close to a heavily watered coastline?

options.option_text: The Konkan coast between Mumbai and Goa, on the windward side
The Malabar Coast in Kerala, which faces the Arabian Sea directly
The interior Deccan Plateau of Maharashtra and northern Karnataka
The Coromandel Coast of Tamil Nadu, facing the Bay of Bengal

questions.explanation: The Western Ghats block moisture-laden SW Monsoon winds; the windward Konkan and Malabar coasts receive 2000–4000 mm annually, while the leeward interior Deccan falls in the rain shadow and receives under 700 mm. Option D (Coromandel Coast) is a trap — it receives rainfall from the retreating NE Monsoon, a completely different mechanism unrelated to the Western Ghats rain shadow.

questions.stem: A river in Peninsular India: (i) originates in the hills of Chhattisgarh; (ii) is dammed by the Hirakud Dam, one of the longest earthen dams in the world; (iii) forms a large delta before draining into the Bay of Bengal through Odisha; and (iv) its basin supports extensive paddy cultivation, earning Odisha the epithet 'Rice Bowl of India'. Identify this river.

options.option_text: Brahmani, which rises in the Garhjat Hills of Odisha
Mahanadi, which originates in the Sihawa hills of Chhattisgarh
Godavari, which rises near Trimbakeshwar in Maharashtra
Baitarani, which originates in the Keonjhar Plateau of Odisha

questions.explanation: All four clues uniquely point to the Mahanadi: it rises in the Sihawa hills of Chhattisgarh, Hirakud Dam (commissioned 1957, ~25 km long) is built across it in Odisha, its large delta and the adjacent Chilika lagoon define coastal Odisha, and its basin is the paddy heartland that earned Odisha the 'Rice Bowl' title. Brahmani (Option A) also flows through Odisha but originates within Odisha itself and is associated with no dam of Hirakud's scale. Godavari has its own independent delta in Andhra Pradesh.

questions.stem:
Consider the following statements about the PHYSIOGRAPHIC DIVISIONS of India:
1. The Great Northern Plains are composed entirely of alluvial deposits from the Indus, Ganga and Brahmaputra river systems.
2. The Peninsular Plateau is the geologically oldest landmass of India, being a remnant of the ancient Gondwana supercontinent.
3. The Western Ghats serve as the main watershed between rivers draining into the Arabian Sea and those draining into the Bay of Bengal.
4. The Eastern Coastal Plains are narrower than the Western Coastal Plains.
Which of the above statements are CORRECT?
questions.explanation: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are all correct: the Great Plains are entirely alluvial; the Peninsular Plateau is a Gondwana fragment and India's oldest stable crustal block; the Western Ghats divide drainage between the Arabian Sea (Narmada, Tapti, short westward rivers) and the Bay of Bengal (Godavari, Krishna, Kaveri). Statement 4 is INCORRECT — the Eastern Coastal Plains (80–100 km wide) are considerably wider than the Western Coastal Plains (10–50 km). Option D is the primary trap for candidates who mark all four statements correct without carefully verifying Statement 4.
